title: When the Portrait Burns Revisited
premise: Retired detective Isandro Quintana discovers that the diary of Marisol Vega—a woman who vanished seven years ago—contains entries written after her disappearance, hidden in a donated book at his failing shop. As he investigates, he learns the diary is being continued by someone who knew her intimately: her sister Elena, who faked the disappearance to escape an abusive husband and has been living in plain sight under a new name. The entries past the vanishing date were Elena's way of keeping Marisol's voice alive—and of leaving breadcrumbs for anyone brave enough to follow. When the husband's family, still powerful in town, moves to have Marisol declared dead and seize her property before the statute expires, Isandro must choose between the law he served for thirty years and the justice it never delivered. In the end, he burns the original portrait of Marisol that hung in the police station—destroying the evidence of her 'death'—and helps Elena disappear properly this time, taking the town's complicity with him into silence.
about_author: Gideon Nystrom is the pen name of a former small-town bookseller who spent a decade cataloguing other people's secrets before writing his own. He lives somewhere coastal, keeps his blinds drawn, and insists every mystery he writes is only half fiction.

chapters.title: The Donation Bin
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Sorting a dead estate's books into his failing shop, Isandro finds a diary wedged inside a hollowed-out atlas—Marisol Vega's, the woman who vanished seven years ago from the town he once policed. The final entry is dated three weeks after she disappeared. The beat is quiet dread: the past knocking on a door he'd nailed shut.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Ghosts
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. He rereads his old case files by lamplight, realizing the investigation was closed too neatly—every alibi polished, every witness rehearsed. A visit to Marisol's sister Elena, now running the town diner, yields nothing but perfect composure. The emotional beat is professional shame: he built the file that buried the truth.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Isandro and the diary itself. The post-disappearance entries describe ordinary days—a market, rain on a window, fear of being found—which means someone alive wrote them. Isandro cross-references handwriting against Elena's diner receipts. The beat is vertigo: the missing woman may never have been missing at all.

chapters.title: The Husband's Family
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The Vega estate is about to pass to Marisol's husband Rodrigo's family under a death declaration, and the statute expires in six weeks. Rodrigo's brother, now a county judge, warns Isandro off with old-fashioned courtesy. The beat is cold recognition: power in this town hasn't changed since his badge came off.

chapters.title: What the Diner Kept
chapters.summary: Elena's POV, first time. She watches Isandro eat breakfast daily, knowing exactly what he's piecing together, remembering the night she drove her sister out of town with a bruised face and a bus ticket. The beat is guarded tenderness: she wants to be caught by someone kind, and fears he isn't that anymore.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibis
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Digging into Rodrigo's history, Isandro finds a pattern stretching back decades—two other women who vanished, two cases he himself helped close. His former partner Tomás admits they were told which questions not to ask. The beat is moral collapse: the corruption wasn't an exception; it was the system he loved.

chapters.title: The Portrait in Evidence
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. In the station basement he finds the official portrait of Marisol—the anchor of the death declaration—along with evidence bags never logged. Someone photographs him leaving. The judge files a harassment complaint, and the bookshop receives its first health inspection in years. The beat is siege: staying invisible was never really an option.

chapters.title: Confession Over Coffee
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. Cornered by Isandro's quiet persistence, Elena finally tells him everything in the diner after closing: the abuse, the escape plan, the diary she kept writing in Marisol's hand so her sister would stay real. The beat is catharsis and terror—trust extended for the first time in seven years, to a man who once failed them both.

chapters.title: Before the Statute Expires
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, climax. With forty-eight hours left, Isandro leaks the unlogged evidence and the pattern of vanishings to a state journalist while Elena prepares to run again—but Rodrigo's family moves first, and Isandro is detained on fabricated charges while Tomás, redeeming himself, smuggles out the last proof. The beat is desperate momentum: justice arriving sideways, through sacrifice.

chapters.title: When the Portrait Burns
chapters.summary: Shared POV, resolution. The state investigation stalls the death declaration; Rodrigo's empire cracks under reopened cases. Isandro, charges dropped, takes the official portrait of Marisol from the evidence shelf and burns it behind his shop—not destroying truth, but freeing her from the town's version of it. Elena leaves on a morning bus, alive and named. The beat is bittersweet peace: some justice lives outside the law, and survival has a price worth paying.
